entries.example: The bed was as hard as iron and I couldn't sleep.
I'll give this plant some water. The soil's dry as a bone.
He's as mad as a hatter*. He crossed the Atlantic in a bathtub.
She told the teacher, as bold as brass, that his lessons were boring.
You'll have to speak slowly and clearly; he's as deaf as a post*.

entries.word: as easy as falling off a log
entries.example: Don't worry. Using the computer's as easy as falling off a log.
She knew the answer as quick as a flash.
When I told him, his face went as red as a beetroot.
The Princess's skin was as white as snow.
When he saw it, his face went as white as a sheet.
The fish was bad and I was as sick as a dog.
She ran off with my money; I felt as sick as a parrot.
I need a drink, I'm as thirsty as can be.
My plan worked like a dream, and the problem was soon solved.
Be careful the boss doesn't see you; she has eyes like a hawk.
He eats like a horse and drinks like a fish*.
Did you sleep well? Yes, thanks, like a log.
Sorry, I forgot to ring him again. I've got a brain/head like a sieve!

entries.word: like a bear with a sore head
entries.example: The boss is like a bear with a sore head today.

entries.word: like a bull in a china shop*
entries.def: [behaving in a very clumsy, insensitive way]
entries.example: She goes around like a bull in a china shop*.

entries.word: like a red rag to a bull
entries.example: Criticising the government in his presence is like a red rag to a bull.
